leads.name: Topola Narutowicza (Narutowicz's Poplar)

location.address: Grounds of Willa Narutowicza, ul. Parkowa 23, Srodmiescie

leads.why_leads_not_shipped: Access, not evidence. The register (via pl.wikipedia's raw wikitext reproduction of Pomniki przyrody w Warszawie, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.4400, designated 2009-08-14, girth 614cm, height 34m) and a dedicated Polish Wikipedia article on Willa Narutowicza (citing Gazeta Wyborcza) together clear the two-source bar easily, and the story is strong: Gabriel Narutowicz, Poland's first president, lived in this villa from his 11 December 1922 swearing-in to his assassination five days later on 16 December, and the poplar named for him still stands on the grounds. But a 2026 web search shows the villa is currently (as of a March 2025 report) being rebuilt into a branch of the Museum of the History of the Polish People's Movement, i.e. an active state-owned construction/renovation site, not a place the public can currently walk onto without permission. No source found states the tree is visible from ul. Parkowa itself. Direct CRFOP fetch was blocked by Incapsula bot protection (crfop.gdos.gov.pl), so nothing further could be checked there this pass. Revisit once the museum work finishes and check for a public entrance, or check street-level visibility (34m poplar may well clear the garden wall) before shipping.
leads.verify_notes: Register + Willa Narutowicza wiki article are solid; only the access test is unresolved. Commons has a dated photo (2019-04-22, File:Topola Narutowicza ul. Parkowa 23.jpg) confirming the tree stood then.

leads.name: Drzewa Romana Witkowskiego (Roman Witkowski's Trees: a ginkgo and a honey locust)
leads.species: Ginkgo (Ginkgo biloba) and Honey Locust (Gleditsia triacanthos)
leads.why_leads_not_shipped: Access uncertain. Register entry (kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.3273, designated 1988-12-28, two species under one designation name) is solid as a single source, matching the established pattern of already-published war_012/war_013 (single-source botanical-garden entries shipped per CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-10 no-single-source-block ruling). But ul. Pilicka 13 is a small plot (773 sqm / 224 sqm building footprint per a Warsaw property record) on a street otherwise described as holding historic villas and at least one embassy; no source found confirms this specific address is a public building, school, or open ground rather than a private residence, which hard rule 10 forbids absolutely regardless of the tree's quality. Nobody identified for certain who Roman Witkowski was. Needs an access check (OSM tag, street view, or a source naming the current occupant) before it can ship.
leads.verify_notes: No independent second source found beyond the register/its Wikipedia reproduction; would ship flagged single-source once access clears, matching war_012/013's precedent.

leads.name: Elm(s) of ul. Belgijska 3 (Wiaz polny / field elm, designated 1983-09-06)
leads.why_leads_not_shipped: Access uncertain. Register (kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.3000, designated 1983-09-06) gives the address but a web search returned an unrelated summary describing '6 common elm trees plus a pear' at this address, which per the search-summary-is-a-lead rule was not trusted or used. Belgijska is a street associated with diplomatic villas in this part of Mokotow; whether this address is a public garden, embassy grounds, or a private residence was not established this pass. Genuinely rare species locally (Dutch elm disease has killed most mature elms in Europe), worth chasing with a direct look rather than a search summary.
leads.verify_notes: Distance to war_009 (already-published Szustra Oaks cluster): roughly 380m, would join the existing Mokotow cluster if access clears.

leads.name: Weeping ash, ul. Pulawska 97 (Jesion wyniosly odm. zwisla)
leads.why_leads_not_shipped: Not verified this pass. Register (kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.3264, designated 1990-12-27, wikitext confirms address ul. Pulawska 97) is a real, single-tree source, but a web search returned a fotopolska.eu page that on direct fetch turned out to document a DIFFERENT ash tree entirely (ul. Pustola, Wola-Ulrychow, kodinspire .3275), which the search's own AI summary had wrongly conflated with this one. Caught before anything was recorded, per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule, but it means no verified second source or photo exists for THIS specific tree yet. Worth a clean re-search next pass, not re-using this one's search terms verbatim.
leads.verify_notes: Would sit roughly 640m from war_009, within the existing Mokotow cluster.
